segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so on Northline, they confirmed 42 seats for the first year, with five admin users. Start date is still June 1 if we can get the order form out today.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Is that the $47,880 annual, net 30, one-year term?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. I put another note on deal desk's approval line this morning, because the quote is still sitting in the CRM draft until that discount field turns green.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Got it. Did they ask for anything weird on terms?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Nothing too odd. They want the SLA attached and the renewal cap at 5%. Legal has the redline from yesterday; I added the clean language in the doc again after lunch, and their procurement guy said he won't countersign while that indemnity sentence is open.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Makes sense. What about billing? I remember they wanted the implementation separate from subscription.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Right, $6,500 services in June and then the subscription invoice July 1. I sent billing the example split again, since the customer is holding the PO until they see the two-line invoice plan match their system.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. If those come back today, can we still book it this month?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, close date is the 30th, and the buyer already confirmed budget. I'll refresh the close plan and keep the next step as order form review.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Cool. Send me the pricing sheet when it's final and I'll check the seat math before it goes out.
